The expected maximum of a simple symmetric random walk of length \(n\) can be expressed exactly as  
\[
\mathbb{E}[M_n] = \mathbb{E}[|S_n|] - \mathbb{P}(S_n \ge 1).
\]
For \(n = 901\) (odd), \(\mathbb{P}(S_{901} \ge 1) = 1/2\) by symmetry, and  
\[
\mathbb{E}[|S_{901}|] = 901 \cdot \binom{900}{450} \big/ 2^{900}.
\]
Using Stirling’s approximation (or the known expansion for the central binomial coefficient) we obtain  
\[
\mathbb{E}[|S_{901}|] \approx 23.95648, \qquad
\mathbb{E}[M_{901}] \approx 23.95648 - 0.5 = 23.45648.
\]
The variance is exactly \(\operatorname{Var}(M_n) = n - \mathbb{E}[M_n] - (\mathbb{E}[M_n])^2\), giving  
\[
\operatorname{Var}(M_{901}) \approx 901 - 23.45648 - (23.45648)^2 \approx 327.337,
\]
so the standard deviation is \(\sigma \approx 18.0925\).

A simulation averages \(N = 4000\) independent copies of \(M_{901}\). The sample mean has standard error  
\[
\sigma / \sqrt{N} \approx 18.0925 / \sqrt{4000} \approx 0.28607.
\]
By the Central Limit Theorem the sample mean is approximately normally distributed with mean \(23.4565\) and standard deviation \(0.2861\).  
We take the point estimate as the median (≈ mean) **23.46**.  
A 50% central interval uses the 75th percentile \(z \approx 0.6745\):  
\(23.4565 \pm 0.6745 \times 0.2861 \approx [23.26,\, 23.65]\).  
A 90% central interval uses \(z \approx 1.645\):  
\(23.4565 \pm 1.645 \times 0.2861 \approx [22.99,\, 23.93]\).

For \(n = 133\):

* \(\log_{10}(133/e) \approx 2.124 - 0.434 = 1.690\)
* \(n\log_{10}(133/e) \approx 133 \times 1.690 = 224.77\)
* \(\frac12\log_{10}(2\pi \times 133) \approx \frac12 \log_{10}(836) \approx \frac12 \times 2.922 = 1.461\)

A more precise calculation (using natural logs and converting) yields \(\log_{10}(133!) \approx 226.16\).

Thus the number of digits is \(\lfloor 226.16 \rfloor + 1 = 227\).
